newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Nine killed as cliff collapses on Australian beach.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Nine killed as cliff collapses on Australian beach.

text.p: Nine people, four adults and five children, were killed on Friday when a 10 metre (30 foot) cliff collapsed on a school group watching a surfing competition at a beach in Western Australia, police said.
"We've completed excavations and we don't expect to find anyone else," police spokesman Tony Potts told Reuters.
"We don't expect the death toll to go any higher," he said.
Police said two people, a young girl and an adult, were hurt but their injuries were not life-threatening.

The schoolchildren, parents and teachers had been marking the last day of the school term with an excursion to a popular surfing beach near Cowaramup National Park about 200 km (120 miles) southwest of Perth, capital of Western Australia.
A police spokesman said the group were sheltering from the wind and rain under the cliffs in the rocky and secluded area.
"(The cliffs) collapsed on top of them and they were buried under tonnes of rubble," he said.
The children in the group, from two local schools, were aged 11 to 13.

"It's a popular spot for all the kids down here to shelter under extreme conditions but it's a very suspect limestone cliff which is very unstable," John Jackovich, who lives near the beach, told state-run Australian Broadcasting Corporation radio.
"It had collapsed a little bit to one side already, about a year ago, and this tragedy now - it's shocking," he said.
"The poor kids wouldn't have had a chance," he said.
Police had earlier feared more bodies would be found under the rubble. All those who died were completely buried by tonnes of rock and sand.
The girl pulled from the rubble was taken to a nearby hospital where her condition was described as satisfactory.
She was the only person pulled from the rubble alive.
Acting deputy Police Commissioner Bruce Brennan told a news conference in Perth the wind and rain had probably eroded the cliff face, causing it to collapse.
